subject: probability-statistics
title: Random variables & discrete distributions
introduction: A random variable turns outcomes into numbers; a PMF tells you how probability is distributed across those numbers. Learn each family by its experiment, not by a detached formula.
theory: Bernoulli models one success/failure trial. Binomial counts successes in a fixed number of independent identical trials. Poisson counts events in a fixed exposure when the rate is stable.
Expectation is linear even without independence. Variances add only when covariance terms vanish.

examples.title: Poisson additivity
examples.solution: $X+Y\sim Pois(5)$, because independent Poisson rates add.

pitfalls: Treating Poisson as continuous—it is discrete.
Using a binomial model when trial probabilities differ.
Assuming linearity of variance the way expectation is linear.
Forgetting that a PMF must sum to one over its full support.
whyGate: These models recur in likelihoods, classifiers, queue/event counts, and the sampling theory used later.
